headline: Wildlife Trade Is in Your Home: 107,356 Species You Didn’t Know About
author: Moby Language Club
text:
Wildlife Trade Is in Your Home: 107,356 Species You Didn’t Know About

Wildlife trade isn't just ivory and rhino horn. A new study from the University of Melbourne, published in Science Advances (October 2026), found that at least 107,356 species of plants, animals and fungi are used and traded worldwide — more than double the previous estimate of around 50,000.

Most of this trade is legal: seafood, timber, furniture, medicinal plants, cut flowers, aquarium fish, exotic pets and mushrooms. In this video, we walk through everyday items in your home and explain why "legal" and "sustainable" aren't the same thing — and what evidence you'd need to judge each one.

Note: The higher number doesn't mean wildlife trade suddenly doubled. It means scientists have now uncovered how much wider the trade has always been.
